ch_priya_1.text: Bed nine asked if I'm married. Then if my sister's married. Then if I have a cousin. He's ninety-one.
I said I'm married to the drug chart. He said the drug chart can't cook. Rude. Accurate, but rude.

choose.text: Did he at least take his tablets?

then.text: Every single one. For me. Apparently that's romance now.

choose.text: I'll do bed nine's round tomorrow.

then.text: You're a hero. A tired, badly dressed hero.

ch_priya_2.text: Grace is doing next month's rota. In pencil. Nobody has ever seen her rubber. Nobody.
If I get four nights in a row again, I'm going to start talking to the drip stands. They're good listeners.

choose.text: Want me to put in a word?

then.text: With Grace? Bold. I'll write your obituary in capital letters.

choose.text: The drip stands do give great advice.

then.text: They do! Stand still, keep dripping. Life lessons.

ch_tom_1.text: Dr. Iyer threw a clip today. Not at anyone. Near someone. Near me.
Twenty years I've been scrubbing. My reflexes are excellent. My heart is not.

choose.text: You caught it, though?

then.text: Caught it, counted it, put it back on the tray. She said thank you. I nearly fainted.

choose.text: Maybe it was a compliment.

then.text: In theatre language, yes. A clip near your head means you're doing fine. A clip at your head, update your CV.

ch_tom_2.text: My daughter wants a laptop for college. A specific one. The one with the fruit on it.
I asked how much. She said, Papa, don't look at the price, look at the vibe. The vibe is two months of my salary.

choose.text: There are cheaper ones that work fine.

then.text: I said that. She said I'm giving budget. I don't know what it means, but I felt attacked.

choose.text: She's going to do great things with it.

then.text: That's what I tell myself. Great things. Also reels. Mostly reels.

ch_grace_1.text: Sit properly. You slouch like an intern who's just been told they're not an intern any more.
Thirty-one years on Ward 4. The building got older, the doctors got younger, and the biscuits got smaller.

choose.text: Thirty-one years. That's a record.

then.text: It's a sentence. With good behaviour I'd have been out in twenty.

choose.text: The biscuits, I believe. The doctors, never.

then.text: Flattery. I'm writing it down. In pencil.

ch_grace_2.text: Do you know why I do the rota in pencil? Because everybody wants to change it, and nobody wants to ask me.
The ones who ask, I say yes. Mostly. The ones who go behind my back get Sundays. Every Sunday. Forever.

choose.text: So the trick is to just ask.

then.text: The trick is to ask nicely. And bring kaju katli. Not the cheap kind.

choose.text: I'm never touching your rota.

then.text: Good. You're learning. Slowly. But learning.

ch_khan_1.text: A man asked me to count backwards from ten in Urdu this morning before I put him to sleep. I did. He was out by seven.
Then he woke up and asked if I was single. Anaesthesia does strange things. Mostly to men.

choose.text: What did you tell him?

then.text: That I'm in a relationship with my monitor. It beeps when it's upset. Very honest.

choose.text: Does that happen a lot?

then.text: Every week. One proposed. One asked for my mother's number. My mother would have said yes.

ch_khan_2.text: Wedding planning is worse than a crash section at three in the morning. At least in theatre people listen to me.
My mother wants four hundred guests. His mother wants six hundred. We are at war over plastic chairs.

choose.text: Elope. Theatre ten is free on Sundays.

then.text: Don't tempt me. The lights are better and nobody's aunty can find it.

choose.text: It'll be beautiful anyway.

then.text: It'll be loud. Beautiful is optional. Loud is guaranteed.

ch_sethi_1.text: I've been awake so long my coffee is drinking me now.
If anyone pages me in the next six hours, tell them I've emigrated. Say Canada. Everyone believes Canada.

choose.text: Go and sleep. I'll take your bleep for an hour.

then.text: You're a terrible liar and a good doctor. I'll take it.

choose.text: Canada needs surgeons too, you know.

then.text: Canada can wait. My bed can't.

ch_sethi_2.text: My mother sent me a biodata. Height, hobbies, blood group. Blood group. In case I need a transfusion on the first date.
Her hobby is travelling. Everyone's hobby is travelling. Nobody's hobby is sitting in a canteen at nine at night.

choose.text: Did you check if you're compatible?

then.text: O positive. Universal donor. Commitment issues, probably.

choose.text: Maybe give it a chance?

then.text: After the exam. And after the next one. There's always a next one.

ch_zoya_1.text: Okay so I accidentally called a consultant bro today. Out loud. To his face.
He said excuse me. I said, sorry sir, bro is gender neutral now. It is not. I made that up on the spot.

choose.text: Did he buy it?

then.text: He said okay, bro. So either we're friends now or I'm fired. Unclear.

choose.text: Maybe save bro for after six.

then.text: Noted. After six, and never to anyone with a lanyard.

ch_zoya_2.text: I have three alarms. One normal, one loud, and one that's just my mother saying my full name.
The third one works every time. Trauma is a powerful motivator.

choose.text: My mum's voice could wake the whole floor.

then.text: See? Mothers are the original pager. No battery, full signal.

choose.text: Maybe go to bed before two?

then.text: Wow. Revolutionary. Next you'll tell me to drink water.

ch_neha_1.text: Dr. Bose sang a whole ghazal during the closing today. Eleven minutes. The patient was asleep. Lucky patient.
I time closings in songs now. A hernia is two ghazals. A gallbladder is three and an encore.

choose.text: And a bowel resection?

then.text: A full concert. With an interval for chai.

choose.text: Ask him for something faster.

then.text: Faster? He doesn't own faster. Even his fast songs are slow.

ch_neha_2.text: Somebody keeps stealing the good scissors from theatre two. I labelled them. They still go missing. With the label.
I'm going to put a tracker on them. Or a curse. Whichever is cheaper.

choose.text: Count me in for the curse.

then.text: Excellent. Midnight, theatre two, bring a swab.

choose.text: Have you checked Tom's pockets?

then.text: Tom's pockets are a museum. Three pens, a bolt, and a samosa from last year. No scissors.

ch_iyer_1.text: Don't look so alarmed. Surgeons are allowed chai. It's in the constitution.
My mother rang. She's decided I should have been a lawyer. She says it isn't too late. I'm fifty-two.

choose.text: You'd have been a terrifying lawyer.

then.text: I'm a terrifying surgeon. Same skill, better lighting.

choose.text: I'm glad you're not.

then.text: So am I. Most days. Don't tell her.

ch_iyer_2.text: The secret of thirty years in surgery? Sit when you can. Eat when you can. Sleep when you can.
And never, ever say it's quiet tonight. The building hears you.

choose.text: I'll never say it.

then.text: Good. Somebody said it in 2009. We had a bus.

choose.text: It is quiet tonight, though.

then.text: Out. Go home. Now. Before something comes through the door.

ch_saxena_1.text: Is it normal for a patient to review me out loud? He said ten on ten, would get appendicitis again.
I told him that's not how appendicitis works. He said manifesting.

choose.text: That's a good day.

then.text: It's my best day. I'm screenshotting it in my brain.

choose.text: Don't let it go to your head.

then.text: Too late. It's already in my head. It's redecorating.

vc_first.text: There you are! We can see you! Can you see us? Anu, move, I can't see myself.
Mum, you don't need to see yourself. That's literally not the point of a video call.
The picture is very clear. This phone was eleven thousand rupees. Every rupee is visible.

choose.text: I miss you all.

then.text: Look at that. Now I'm crying, and the camera can see it. Eleven thousand rupees of crying.

choose.text: Dad, why is your camera pointing at the fan?

then.text: It's a new angle. Very modern. Anu set it.
I did not.

vc_first.text: Are you eating? You look thin. The camera adds weight and you still look thin.

vc_loss.text: You're quiet. You're never quiet on the phone. You were quiet when you were six and broke the mixie.
Somebody didn't make it today, na. You don't have to tell me. I can hear it.

choose.text: We lost a patient today.

then.text: Then you'll eat something, you'll sleep, and tomorrow you'll go back. Sad, and then back. That's the job, na?

choose.text: Just tired, Mum.

then.text: Tired. Okay. Tired people eat too. I'll stay on the line till you eat something. I've waited longer for less.

vc_loss.text: Your father wants to say something. He won't. But he wants to. That counts.

vc_promoted.text: Promoted! I've told Gupta uncle, the milkman, and two people at the bank who didn't ask.
He's printed your photo on the office colour printer. His boss thinks it's a wanted poster.

choose.text: Thank you for always believing in me.

then.text: Believing? I had no choice. Your school fees were non-refundable.
He cried. In the car. Twice.

choose.text: Dad, please don't print any more photos.

then.text: Too late. Laminated. Fridge, office, and my wallet.

vc_after_visit.text: Mum went to your hospital? Like, physically? With a tiffin? I'm screaming.
She's told the whole building it's a five star hospital. She also said one of the nurses was very strict. Which one?

choose.text: Sister Grace. Please never repeat that.

then.text: The one with the pencil? Mum says she's a very strong lady. That's Mum for terrifying.

choose.text: Honestly, it was iconic.

then.text: I know. She's already planning the next visit. With pickle. In a glass jar. Be afraid.

vc_food.text: What did you eat today? And don't say chai. Chai is not food. Chai is a feeling.
I'm sending a parcel with Gupta uncle's son. Thepla, pickle, and the laddoos you pretend you don't like.

choose.text: You're the best, Mum.

then.text: I know. Share the laddoos with the nurses. Not all. Some. The good nurses.

choose.text: I had biscuits. Three. That counts.

then.text: Three biscuits. My child is a doctor and eats like a sparrow. I'm sending double.

vc_forwards.text: Did you get my forward? The one about turmeric curing everything. It has a doctor in it. A real one. With a coat.
Seventy-two thousand people forwarded it. They can't all be wrong.

choose.text: Turmeric's lovely in dal, Dad. It doesn't cure cancer.

then.text: Hmm. I'll keep it in the dal, then. Don't tell your mother. She's already put it in the milk.

choose.text: Please stop forwarding those to the family group.

then.text: Free speech. Also, your aunty forwards worse. She sent one about onions in socks.

vc_forwards.text: Okay, okay. You're the doctor. I'm only the father who paid for the doctor.

vc_anu_fest.text: Emergency. Not medical. Worse. College fest is next week and Mum says I should just wear something from your cupboard.
Your cupboard is ninety percent scrubs. I'm not going to my fest dressed as a ward. Huge respect. Not the vibe.

choose.text: I'll send you money for something new.

then.text: This is why you're the favourite. Don't tell Mum. Actually, tell Mum. She should know.

choose.text: Scrubs are very comfortable, actually.

then.text: Comfortable is not a personality. Okay, boomer. Doctor boomer.

vc_anu_fest.text: I'm listening, you know. Both of you. Eat something.

vc_rishta.text: Sharma aunty has found someone for you. Software, Pune, owns a car, owns two plants, both alive.
I told her our child is a doctor, there's no time. She said, then when? I said after the next promotion. I've been saying that for years.

choose.text: Mum, I'm married to the job for now.

then.text: The job doesn't call me on Sundays. The job doesn't eat my rajma. Fine. I'll tell her you're focusing.

choose.text: Ask if the plants want to meet first.

then.text: See? This is why nobody can arrange anything for you. Too smart. Too funny. Eat something.

vc_neighbour.text: Mrs. Kulkarni from downstairs has a pain in her knee. I told her you'll look at it. On video. Now.
She's literally standing behind Mum holding her knee up to the camera. I'm so sorry.

choose.text: Show me the knee, aunty. Can you bend it?

then.text: See? Free consultation. She's brought pakoras for you. I'll freeze them. They'll be terrible.

choose.text: Mum, I can't examine knees on a video call.

then.text: Then what is this phone for? Eleven thousand rupees and it can't do knees.

vc_neighbour.text: Aunty says you're very confident for your age. That's a compliment, from her. Take it.

lf_mum_visit.text: There you are! No call for days. Days! I thought, either you're very busy or very dead. So I came to check which.
I brought rajma. Hot. In the steel dabba. Don't make that face. Everybody can see you making that face.

choose.text: Mum! You came all this way?

then.text: Two buses and an auto. The auto driver knows your whole life now. He says congratulations.

choose.text: Mum, I'm working. On a ward. With patients.

then.text: And I'm your mother. On a ward. With rajma. Both things can be true.
Aunty, visiting hours are four to six. But rajma is welcome at the nurses' desk any time.

lf_mum_visit.text: See? Very nice lady. A bit strict. Call me tonight. Every night. Or next time I'm bringing your father. And his forwards.

pt_hostel.text: Look who it is! The government hospital legend. Still living on canteen samosas? I'd hug you, but this shirt is linen.
CarePlus gave me my own parking spot. With my name on it. In gold. Well, gold coloured.

choose.text: Congratulations on the parking spot.

then.text: Thank you. You can visit it sometime. Not park in it. Visit.

choose.text: Do they let you operate, or just park?

then.text: Wow. Okay. Wow.

pt_hostel.text: Carrom. You and me. Loser buys chai for the whole batch. I've been practising. On an app.

then.text: That board is tilted. I'm reporting this board. Fine. Chai's on me. Small cups.

else.text: Like I said. App training. I'm posting this. Hashtag CarePlus excellence.

pt_hostel.text: Honestly, though. This is nice. Nobody at CarePlus plays carrom. They play squash. I hate squash.

pt_diwali.text: Diwali on the terrace. Thirty years, and the fire brigade has only come twice.
No rockets this year. Last year Tom's rocket went into the ICU window. The patient said it was the best Diwali of his life.
He did say that. I have it in writing.
Antakshari! Nurses against doctors. Losers wash the sweet boxes. All of them. Even the sticky ones.

then.text: The doctors won. Write down the date. It won't happen again.

else.text: Nurses win. As always. The sweet boxes are in the corner, Doctor. Sticky side up.

pt_diwali.text: That's your pager. On Diwali. Of course it is.

choose.text: I'll go. Save me a kaju katli.

then.text: One kaju katli. Guarded with my life. Okay, with Tom's life.

choose.text: Casualty can manage one burn.

then.text: Can it? Casualty tonight is two nurses and a man with a mop.

pt_grace.text: Surprise! Okay, it's not a surprise. She found the cake at four. She's been pretending not to know for three hours.
I don't do birthdays. Birthdays are for people with time. I have a ward.
Sister Grace, it's literally a vibe though. There's a cake. With your face on it. Printed.
My face. On a cake. And who is going to cut my face?
Speech! The doctor gives the speech. Doctors love talking. It's in the training.

then.text: Well. That was adequate. Very adequate. Somebody give the doctor the piece with my eyebrow.
Thank you. Short. I like short. Like doctors' handwriting, but readable.

else.text: That was a speech. Technically. Cut the cake before anyone else talks.

choose.text: I'll do it. Keep my slice safe.

then.text: Leaving my party for my ward. Correct answer. I'll cut you a big piece. Not the face.

choose.text: Bed three can wait ten minutes.

then.text: My ward does not wait ten minutes. Not even on my birthday. I'll do it myself. Happy birthday to me.

pt_khan.text: You came! Eat first. There are three biryanis and a war between two mothers. Pick a side carefully.
Surprise. The groom is my cousin. Small world. Small, unfair world.
My husband's cousin. I found out at the engagement. I've made my peace with it. Mostly.
Dance-off. You and me. The family wants a show. My aunt has already started filming.

then.text: I tore something. A ligament or my pride. Don't examine either.
Best wedding present so far. Better than the four pressure cookers.

else.text: And that's how it's done. Aunties, did you get that? Family group. Now.
You did your best. Your best was enthusiastic.

choose.text: I'm sorry. I have to go.

then.text: Go. Take biryani. A doctor who leaves a wedding for a patient is the only kind I'd invite.

choose.text: Tonight, I'm a guest.

then.text: Then dance, guest. The appendix has other doctors. You only get one of my weddings. Hopefully.

pt_rao.text: Thirty-four years, and nobody has ever seen him without that pen. Tonight he's put it down. It's unsettling.
Please. No speeches. I hate speeches. Especially ones about me.
Which is why the new Head of Department is giving one. Go on. You've been volunteered. By me.

then.text: I said no speeches. That one I'll allow. Write it down for me. I'll read it when the pension office is rude.
Thank you. Short and true. Like a good operation.

else.text: You'll be a fine Head of Department. Speeches aren't in the job description. Thank God.

pt_rao.text: Sorry, sorry, am I late? CarePlus sent flowers. And me. Mostly the flowers.
Dr. Khanna. Your hospital sends flowers to my farewell, and a junior to count the chairs. Very CarePlus.
I am not counting the chairs. I counted them in the car. There are forty.

choose.text: Stay, Varun. Have a samosa.

then.text: Really? Okay. Our canteen does quinoa. I miss samosas. Don't tell anyone.

choose.text: The door's where you left it.

then.text: Harsh. Fair, but harsh. The flowers stay, though. They were expensive.

pt_rao.text: {called}. Look after Ward 4. And look after Meera. She won't let you, so do it quietly.

pt_carrom_night.text: Carrom. Me against the Chief. If I win, I get Sunday off. If you win, I'll still ask for Sunday off.
I'm keeping score. I'm also streaming this to the intern group. Twelve people are watching. Thirteen. Hi, Mummy.

then.text: Okay, that was clean. Respect. I'm still asking for Sunday.

else.text: Sunday off, Chief. You said. On stream. Thirteen witnesses.

pt_antakshari_night.text: Antakshari night! Nurses against doctors. We're unbeaten since Diwali. Mostly. Shh.
Same rules. No repeats, no humming, and no pretending a song exists when it doesn't, Dr. Qureshi.

then.text: The doctors won? Who taught you songs? Was it the radio? It was the radio.

else.text: Nurses win! Sweet boxes, Chief. You know where they are.

pt_sangeet_night.text: My cousin's sangeet. You're invited because my mother wanted to see a real Chief. Be impressive. Or at least tall.
Before you ask, no, nobody invited me. I always come. It's a gift.
Dance-off. Chief against the uninvited man. The dhol is ready. I am so ready.

then.text: Fine. You win. I'm going to eat four gulab jamuns and process this.

else.text: Undefeated at weddings I wasn't invited to. Write it on my hoarding.

choose.text: Casualty needs me. Sorry, Neha.

then.text: Go, go. My mother is now more impressed, not less. You've ruined it for every future guest.

choose.text: The registrar can handle a fish bone.

then.text: Correct. Fish bones are character building. For registrars.
